metadata.project: HeatSense — Statistical Identification of High-Temperature Risk
metadata.source: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API / ECMWF ERA5

sample_metrics.cv_interpretation_warning: Celsius is an interval temperature scale with an arbitrary zero point (0°C = 273.15 K). Therefore, presenting CV = (s / mean_C) * 100% as a physically meaningful relative variability percentage is statistically invalid, as its numerical value changes arbitrarily under affine shifts. On the true ratio Kelvin scale, relative dispersion is 0.79% (s / mean_K, where mean_K = 303.39 K).

secular_trend.partial_year_disclosure: 2026 (partial record through Oct 10, excluded from annual trend to prevent seasonal bias)

model_selection.goodness_of_fit_diagnostic: A model possessing the lowest AIC among candidates does NOT mean it provides a good absolute fit. Formal Kolmogorov-Smirnov goodness-of-fit testing rejects all candidate single distributions (p < 0.0001) due to strong annual seasonal cycles (cold winters vs. hot summers). The best candidate (lognorm) serves only as a relative parametric approximation; the empirical exceedance rate (0.95%) is the primary, directly verifiable baseline.

heat_risk_index_audit.status: Exploratory uncalibrated operational decision support score (0-100 scale)
heat_risk_index_audit.audit_notice: index_score (0-100) = [empirical_exceedance_rate * (1 + trend_adjustment) * (1 + clustering_adjustment)] * 100. This metric is an exploratory composite decision-support indicator, NOT a formal calibrated statistical probability.
